# Customize icon set

`Theme` supplies the icon set, and you customize it through its `icons` prop. Without `icons`, a top-level `Theme` uses `defaultIcons`, and a nested `Theme`, for example one that only sets `colorScheme`, keeps the icons of the surrounding one.

## Replace some icons

Pass the URLs of your SVG files to `Theme`. Spread `defaultIcons` first, so every icon you don't replace stays the one of `@dextinity/ui`:

<Canvas of={CustomizeIconSetStories.ReplaceSomeIcons} />

## Replace all icons

Leave the spread out. `icons` must then list every icon, so a missing one is a type error. Use this only when your project has its own icon style, so that no icon of `@dextinity/ui` shows up in a different style.

There is a risk: `@dextinity/ui` may add new icons in a minor version. Every new icon is then a type error in your project until you add your own version of it.

```tsx
<Theme
    icons={{
        "arrow-right": arrowRightUrl,
        favorite: favoriteUrl,
        // … every other icon
    }}
>
```

## Add icons

Add the name to `IconRegistry` through module augmentation, then pass its URL to `Theme`:

```ts
declare module "@dextinity/ui" {
    interface IconRegistry {
        "my-icon": true;
    }
}
```

```tsx
<Theme icons={{ ...defaultIcons, "my-icon": myIconUrl }}>
    <Icon icon="my-icon" />
</Theme>
```

Every `Theme` that sets `icons` must then include `"my-icon"`, or it's a type error.

## Prepare an SVG file

- The root element is `<svg id="icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">`. `Icon` shows the element with the id `icon`, and only a 16×16 `viewBox` fits.
- An icon drawn in one color uses `currentColor` for that color, so it takes the text color.
- An icon drawn in one color uses no masks and no gradients. Safari ignores both in a file that `<use>` loads: a gradient isn't drawn, and a mask isn't applied. Redraw the shape without them, or give it fixed colors instead of `currentColor` and mark it with `hasOwnColors` (see "Icons with their own colors"). It then no longer takes the text color.
- Get its URL from your bundler with `new URL("./icons/my-icon.svg#icon", import.meta.url).href`, which works in Vite and Next.js. Keep `#icon` at the end: without it, Vite puts a small SVG file into the JS bundle as a `data:` URL, which `<use>` can't load.

## Icons with their own colors

An icon with its own colors, such as a brand logo, is marked with `hasOwnColors`. `Icon` shows it as an image, which keeps its colors and gradients in every browser:

```tsx
<Theme icons={{ ...defaultIcons, "my-logo": { url: myLogoUrl, hasOwnColors: true } }}>
```
